open_points.subject: data_provider dependency
open_points.text: The dependency stack places `models, data_provider` on one line and says “modules on one line do not know each other,” but `data_provider` now says “Knows `models`.”
open_points.question: May `data_provider` depend on `models`, and if so how is the dependency stack changed or excepted?
options: Create an explicit exception allowing `data_provider` to know `models` despite sharing its line
Remove the dependency by representing table keys and cells without importing model enumerations

open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: “the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7)” describes a table keyed only by NodeExecution status, while `outcome_unknown` can mean waiting, succeeded, or failed with `applied_outputs_unknown` depending on the related EffectAttempt and binding outputs.
open_points.question: What cell does `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` contain for `outcome_unknown`, and how must `run_graph` combine it with the EffectAttempt resolution and binding outputs?
options: Use a distinct context-dependent/deferred conclusion member and let `run_graph` resolve it through `effects.operation_element_conclusion`
Exclude `outcome_unknown` from this table, contradicting the requirement that it be total
Map it to waiting and let another explicit override replace that conclusion after resolution
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct context-dependent conclusion member that `run_graph` resolves using `effects.operation_element_conclusion`.

open_points.subject: conclusion correspondence taxonomies
open_points.text: “a table here keyed by the enumeration, total over its members, whose cells name members” introduces `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` and `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS`, but the texts define no NodeConclusion enumeration, no node-effect enumeration, and no cell structure for the separate effects on the run and on dependants.
open_points.question: What are the exact row-key enumeration, cell enumeration or record shape, and complete member-to-member values of `EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS` and `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS`?
options: Add explicit NodeConclusion and NodeConclusionEffect enumerations and list every table row
Use structured cells containing separate run and dependant dispositions and define their closed member sets
Use existing status enumerations directly and explicitly list how each status maps on both axes
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit conclusion and disposition enumerations, with structured `NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS` cells for run and dependant behavior, and list every row.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: “whether an HTTP method carries a body” is required to be a table “whose cells name members,” but no body/no-body enumeration or cell type is defined.
open_points.question: What exact cell type and complete mapping must `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` expose for `GET`, `DELETE`, `POST`, `PUT`, and `PATCH`?
options: A boolean mapping, with `GET` and `DELETE` false and the other methods true
A new closed body-disposition enumeration with `no_body` and `body` members
A mapping to an existing request-shape taxonomy, if one is intended
open_points.default_guess: Use a boolean mapping: `GET` and `DELETE` false; `POST`, `PUT`, and `PATCH` true.
